page: Microsoft Azure M96bds_2_v3 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C x86_64 processor with 48 physical cores and 96 virtual CPUs running at a dedicated speed of 4.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1946.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 20.27 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with 4608 GB of capacity, and the instance is premium storage capable. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance across multiple categories. The instance achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth, reaching 7459.57 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 429.2 GB/sec for large-block reads. Multi-threaded operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a bzip3 decompression speed of 559.33 GB/sec and a Passmark CPU score of 97234.14. Single-core performance is average to strong, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2056.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2195.0. Database operations are highly optimized, scoring 35122.57 on Passmark database tests and executing 114.97 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M96bds_2_v3 offers high resource density, combining massive memory capacity with substantial local storage and dedicated high-frequency compute resources. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, large-scale databases, and heavy multi-threaded processing. However, a potential tradeoff is the lack of a dedicated GPU, which limits its efficiency for heavy parallel graphics rendering or native GPU-accelerated deep learning, though it maintains strong CPU-based LLM inference capabilities, processing 256.77 tokens per second for medium 7B models. It is best suited for in-memory databases, large-scale data compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
